project.objective: Who were the parents of Reuben Spencer Spriggs, born 6 November 1898 in Maddock, Benson County, North Dakota?

questions.question: Who were the parents of Reuben Spencer Spriggs, born 6 November 1898 in Maddock, Benson County, North Dakota?
questions.rationale: This is the project's sole objective, restated as a single-fact relationship question. Reuben has no parent links in the tree. Benson County, North Dakota was organized by 1898, and vital records, territorial/state census records, and federal census records from the late 1890s through the 1910s plausibly cover the area. The 1900 federal census would show the household in which Reuben (then ~18 months old) was enumerated, directly naming his parents. The 1910 census and North Dakota state records may further corroborate. His WWI draft registration and 1915 South Dakota state census (showing him as 'Spencer Spriggs') suggest he left North Dakota before 1915, making early-period Benson County records the primary target.

exhaustive_declaration.justification: All 11 plan items in pl_001 are completed. Two independent federal census records (1910 and 1920) place Reuben Spencer Spriggs and his siblings in the household of John W./Will Spriggs (b. ~1872, Iowa) and Charlotte/Charlott Spriggs (b. Norway, immigrated 1877) in Beadle County, South Dakota. The 1880 Iowa census corroborates the father's identity and origin. All relevant repositories were searched: 1900, 1910, 1915 ND censuses (negative — family absent from ND); ND county marriages; ND naturalization; BLM GLO land records; WWI draft cards; Benson County Lutheran church records (Esmond and Flora, indexed); SSDI; GenealogyBank obituaries; ND Pioneer Files. North Dakota statewide birth registration began in 1907 (FamilySearch wiki, North Dakota Vital Records), nine years after Reuben's 1898 birth; county-level records are not held by FamilySearch. Baptism was the decisive record to gate on; both Benson County church collections were searched with 0 indexed results. The SS-5 application (requiring Ancestry or SSA FOIA request, not accessible through available tools) would be corroborative but is not the sole available evidence. No conflicts exist. Overturn risk is low given two independent enumeration events confirming the same household composition.

stop_criteria.goal_alignment: Met. The 1910 US Census (src_004, log_029) directly records 'Rueben S Spriggs' as son of John W. Spriggs (head, b. 1872, Iowa) and Charlotte Spriggs (wife, b. Norway) in Prairie Belle, Beadle County, SD. The 1920 census (src_003, log_030) corroborates with sibling Spencer Spriggs (b. ~1899, ND) in the same household under Will/Charlott Spriggs. A convincing, specific answer is in hand: father is J. William/John W./Will Spriggs (I4, b. ~1872, Iowa) and mother is Charlotte/Charlott Spriggs (I7, b. Norway, immigrated 1877).
stop_criteria.repository_breadth: Met. Searched: 1900 federal census (Benson County and all ND, negative); 1910 federal census (all ND, negative — family had relocated to SD); 1915 ND state census (all ND, negative); 1920 federal census (found in Beadle County, SD); 1880 federal census (found in Winneshiek, Iowa); ND county marriages 1872-2000 (negative); ND naturalization records — two indexed collections plus Benson County volumes (negative); BLM GLO tract books (negative for father in ND); WWI draft cards (17 results, none matching); Benson County church records, Esmond and Flora Lutheran volumes (negative, indexed portion); SSDI (confirms subject); GenealogyBank obituaries (negative); ND Pioneer Files (negative, different family). FAN cluster pursued through siblings Spencer and Leonard Spriggs in 1920 census. All relevant repositories, jurisdictions, and name variants tried.
stop_criteria.original_substitution: Met. Census records accessed as original records via FamilySearch ark image links (ark:/61903/1:1:MPXD-MZC, ark:/61903/1:1:M6N2-M3W, ark:/61903/1:1:MDL5-8P4). The SS-5 application (original) was not accessible through available tools; the SSDI (index/derivative) was used in its place to confirm subject identity. This limitation is noted but does not block declaration given the census originals establish parentage directly.
stop_criteria.independent_verification: Met. Three independent sources from different record-creation events: (1) 1910 US Census (src_004) — Reuben listed as son of John W. and Charlotte Spriggs; (2) 1920 US Census (src_003) — sibling Spencer Spriggs (b. ~1899, ND) independently corroborates the same household composition under Will/Charlott Spriggs; (3) 1880 US Census (src_002) — establishes J. William Spriggs (b. ~1872, Iowa) as child of John W. and Emma J. Spriggs, confirming the father's identity chain. The 1910 and 1920 censuses are separate enumeration events with different enumerators; they are independent sources, not a single informant repeated.
stop_criteria.evidence_class: Met, with notation. The 1910 US Census (src_004) is an original record accessed via FamilySearch ark image. It records primary information for residence/enumeration facts and indeterminate information for the parentage relationship (household member respondent, unknown). No birth certificate or baptism record is available: North Dakota statewide birth registration did not begin until 1907 (per FamilySearch wiki, North Dakota Vital Records), nine years after Reuben's November 1898 birth; the FamilySearch Library has not acquired ND birth records; both Benson County church collections (Esmond and Flora) returned 0 indexed results. The 1910 census is the best original record available for this jurisdiction and period. This is an indirect-evidence parentage case, not a direct primary parentage record case.
stop_criteria.conflict_resolution: Met. No registered conflicts exist (conflicts section returns 0 items). The 1-year birth-year variance (1899 in 1910 census vs. 1898 per SSDI/tree) is explained by census rounding — a child born November 1898 enumerated April 1910 at age 11 is consistent with either year. The name variants 'Rueben S' / 'Spencer Spriggs' vs. 'Reuben Spencer Spriggs' are standard orthographic variations. The name variants 'John W.' / 'J. William' / 'Will Spriggs' for the father across three censuses (1880, 1910, 1920) are reconciled by birthplace (Iowa), birth year (~1872), and family composition. No substantive discrepancies remain unresolved.
stop_criteria.overturn_risk: Low. Two independent census enumerations (1910 and 1920) in different locations confirm the same parental household. The SS-5 application — the most likely source to contain a direct parental statement — is corroborative in nature and not accessible through available tools (Ancestry/SSA FOIA required); its absence does not undermine the conclusion. The unindexed portion of Benson County church records is a theoretical gap, but the family surname is English (not Norwegian), the family relocated from ND before 1915, and no baptism record would plausibly name different parents than those already confirmed by two census records. All known record types that could contradict the conclusion have been searched and returned negative or consistent results.

items.rationale: The father of Reuben Spencer Spriggs may have filed a homestead claim in Benson County (Maddock area) around the time of Reuben's 1898 birth; homesteading in North Dakota was most active 1880s-1900s. FamilySearch collection 2074276 (United States, Bureau of Land Management Tract Books, name-searchable (personCount 7493413)) covers this period; BLM application files can name the claimant's birthplace and state or country of origin. The locality guide (loc_001) specifically recommends BLM GLO records as a free, accessible source. Date range set to parents' plausible homesteading window, based on parents born approximately 1860-1882.

If either parent was an immigrant (Benson County had substantial Scandinavian and central-European immigration per loc_001), naturalization papers would name the applicant's birthplace and origin, and witnesses were often relatives or neighbors. Search FamilySearch collection 3241359 (North Dakota, Naturalization Records, 1868-1924, name-searchable (personCount 1887)) and 3241319 (North Dakota and South Dakota Naturalization Records, 1851-1924, name-searchable (personCount 6835)). If both are negative, follow with a full-text search of the Benson County naturalization volumes (imageGroups 007785641-007785645), which are full-text searchable but NOT name-indexed per loc_001 quirk.

quirks: Benson County was organized March 9, 1883 from DeSmet and Ramsey counties (Dakota Territory). Records predating 1883 for this territory are filed under those predecessor counties — search Ramsey County (Dakota Territory) first for pre-1883 events.
The 1890 federal census for Benson County is entirely destroyed. Substitute with the 1885 Dakota Territory census, the 1885 and 1915 North Dakota state censuses, and county tax records.

County-level birth registration began only in the late 1890s; statewide registration did not begin until 1907 with general compliance by 1924. A birth certificate for an 1898 birth may not exist — request directly from the Benson County Courthouse (Minnewaukan, ND 58351; 701-473-5345) to confirm.

County-level death registration begins 1895; statewide death registration began 1907 with general compliance by 1924. The FamilySearch Library has not acquired any North Dakota state birth or death records.

Statewide marriage registration did not begin until 1925; pre-1925 marriages are county-level only. The Benson County Courthouse holds marriage records from the late 1800s; FamilySearch collection 2550852 covers 1872-2000.

The Benson County naturalization volumes (imageGroups 007785641-007785645, ~3,570 images total) are full-text searchable at FamilySearch but are NOT name-indexed — use the FamilySearch full-text search interface or browse image by image. Cross-check first with the indexed collections 3241359 and 3241319.

The Esmond and Flora Lutheran church record volumes (imageGroups 100881428 and 100881427) are only 34-36% name-indexed. Norwegian-language entries are common — researchers must be prepared to read or translate Norwegian script and browse unindexed images.
No courthouse disasters are on record for Benson County; the FamilySearch Wiki states explicitly there is no known history of courthouse disasters there.

The Spirit Lake (Devils Lake) Indian Reservation lies primarily in Benson County (with a portion in Eddy County). Federal Indian Agency records (Fort Totten) run in a separate series — imageGroups 008271676 and 008273622 — and are full-text searchable but not name-indexed.

Benson County borders Eddy (south), Nelson (east), Pierce (north), Ramsey (northeast), Towner (northwest), and Wells (west). Families near county lines may have marriage, church, or land records in neighboring counties — search all adjoining county record sets if Benson County records are negative.

The 1900 federal census (Benson County volume, imageGroup 004120517_002_M9LK-PZ1, 92% indexed) is the highest-priority record for identifying the parents of Reuben Spencer Spriggs (b. 6 Nov 1898). He should appear at approximately age 18 months in his parents' household at the June 1900 enumeration.

Local Maddock-area newspapers from the late 1890s routinely published birth notices and may be the only surviving record of Reuben's 1898 birth naming his parents. Contact the State Historical Society of North Dakota (http://history.nd.gov/archives/whatnewspapers.html) to identify and locate relevant issues.

BLM General Land Office homestead records (https://glorecords.blm.gov) are free and may name Reuben's father or grandfather as a homestead claimant; application files can include birthplace and origin information.
